$description: Curated OFL-1.1 families for HouseOS themes, each checked against the Fontsource API (exists, licence OFL, subsets include latin-ext) on 2026-09-26 (the last twelve on 2026-09-27); kb_400 is the latin + latin-ext woff2 size of weight 400 normal (budget: fonts/ ≤ 800 KB per theme), axes lists variable axes beyond wght/ital.

fonts.character: Bundled. A jacquard-loom blackletter drawn on a 12-unit pixel grid: gothic, woven, crisp at multiples of 12 px.
fonts.avoid: Any size that is not a multiple of 12; anything longer than a title; all-caps runs.

fonts.character: Bundled. A calligraphic humanist sans with real italics and small x-height; bookish, warm, never corporate.
fonts.avoid: Weights under 400 on dark grounds; tight tracking.

fonts.character: Bundled. Engineered, slightly mechanical mono with a friendly italic; reads as instrument panel, not hacker cliché.
fonts.avoid: Using it for body copy to look 'technical'.

fonts.character: Adobe's workhorse humanist: calm, open counters, excellent French diacritics; the quiet body under a loud display.
fonts.avoid: Pairing it with another neutral sans; it needs a characterful partner.

fonts.character: Built for small phone screens (Firefox OS): sturdy, slightly technical humanist with a big family.
fonts.avoid: Hairline weights; it is heavy per weight (≈70 KB), budget files.

fonts.character: Braille Institute's legibility face, expanded: distinct Il1, 0O, exaggerated forms; odd in a good, honest way.
fonts.avoid: Display sizes: its quirks become clumsy above ~32 px.

fonts.character: The original two-weight Atkinson: blunt, friendly, unmistakable letterforms for low-vision readers.
fonts.avoid: Needing a 500/600 step: use Atkinson Hyperlegible Next instead.

fonts.character: Geometric-leaning sans tuned for reading fluency (wide spacing); clean but not sterile at heavy weights.
fonts.avoid: Pairing with a geometric display: two circles-and-lines faces flatten each other.

fonts.character: SIL's face for beginning readers: single-storey a, clear shapes; school-primer warmth, huge language coverage.
fonts.avoid: Weight budget (≈100 KB per weight); only 400/700 exist.

fonts.character: Olivia King's accessible sans: humanist warmth with legibility quirks, contemporary without being startup-shiny.
fonts.avoid: Weights under 400.

fonts.character: Ink-trapped French grotesque with optical sizes and width: tight and punchy large, open small; poster energy.
fonts.avoid: Its narrow width at text size; keep opsz automatic.

fonts.character: Scandinavian grotesque with idiosyncratic curves (the g, the y): household, a little odd, very human.
fonts.avoid: Using it with another quirky sans.

fonts.character: Newsroom grotesque from a Norwegian media house: compact, sturdy, confident in headlines and lists.
fonts.avoid: Light weights; it wants to be set 400–800.

fonts.character: Crisp, slightly condensed neo-grotesque with a width axis; precise, editorial, gallery-label cool.
fonts.avoid: Using it alone: it is neutral enough to read as 'default'.

fonts.character: Revival of Franklin Gothic: American newspaper and signage grotesque, blunt at black weight, plain at 400.
fonts.avoid: Thin weights (100–300): out of character.

fonts.character: Grotesque with a width axis from condensed to expanded: one family can give a tall narrow display and a calm body.
fonts.avoid: Mixing more than two widths in one theme.

fonts.character: GitHub's strong grotesque with a width axis; industrial, square-shouldered at wide/black.
fonts.avoid: Its wide black at small sizes; developer-conference clichés.

fonts.character: Futura's open-source cousin: 1920s geometric, Bauhaus posters, métro lettering; pointed apexes, round o.
fonts.avoid: Long paragraphs at 300; very tight tracking.

fonts.character: Vintage geometric with a tiny x-height and wide caps: Art Deco, Scandinavian 1930s, elegant but short.
fonts.avoid: Body text: its x-height is too small for reading.

fonts.character: Art-centre face that widens dramatically with weight; avant-garde, loud at 800, oddly cute at 500.
fonts.avoid: Body and controls; mid weights at small sizes.

fonts.character: Wonky 'Old Style Soft' with optical size and SOFT/WONK axes: warm, literary, a little mischievous, 1970s book jackets.
fonts.avoid: Its WONK axis and SOFT 100 at body sizes; the 9pt opsz at display.

fonts.character: Claude Garamont's 16th-century roman, faithfully revived: French humanist book text, true italics, old-style figures.
fonts.avoid: Small UI text on dark grounds (thin hairlines); ≈80 KB per weight.

fonts.character: High-contrast, sharp display Garamond: luxurious, cold, fashion-magazine; beautiful large, brittle small.
fonts.avoid: Anything below 24 px; weight 300 on screens.

fonts.character: Caslon for screens: 18th-century English print, pamphlets, almanacs; slightly heavy, trustworthy, bookish.
fonts.avoid: Needing more than 400/700.

fonts.character: Production Type's screen-news serif with optical sizes: calm reading, crisp headlines, a Sunday paper.
fonts.avoid: Light weights on dark grounds.

fonts.character: Production Type's quiet screen serif: sharp wedges, long lines, restrained, a museum catalogue.
fonts.avoid: Heavy display use; it is a text face.

fonts.character: Dynamic, calligraphic literary serif designed with Alegreya Sans: a superfamily with the bundled body.
fonts.avoid: Mixing it with another serif.

fonts.character: 'Wholemeal' serif: dark, robust, rustic; black weight looks like woodcut almanac titles.
fonts.avoid: Light-on-dark small sizes at 400 look heavy; loosen line height.

fonts.character: Revival of a 1918 Polish state-print face: interwar Central Europe, stamps, banknotes, civic warmth.
fonts.avoid: Using it to fake 'medieval'; it is 20th-century.

fonts.character: Condensed, high-contrast display serif with a lovely italic: gallery walls, perfume labels, restraint.
fonts.avoid: Body or labels; bold (none exists, never fake it).

fonts.character: Heavy 1970s old-style: rounded wedges, soft blackness; cookbooks, record sleeves, warm kitchens.
fonts.avoid: Small sizes; pairing with Fraunces (same era, one too many).

fonts.character: Dramatic, ink-trapped high-contrast serif: nightclub posters, literary magazines, sharp elegance.
fonts.avoid: Anything under 24 px; its hairlines vanish.

fonts.character: Contemporary slab made for screens: sturdy, low contrast, very readable; typewriter-adjacent without cosplay.
fonts.avoid: Weights under 400; pairing with another slab.

fonts.character: Mozilla's slab: squarish, bookish-techy, a little cheeky in its italics.
fonts.avoid: Mixing with Bitter or Besley.

fonts.character: Clarendon revival: bracketed slabs, ball terminals, Victorian posters and seed packets, warm and assertive.
fonts.avoid: Italic for long text; tight line height at body.

fonts.character: Single heavy slab: circus bills, wanted posters, ticket booths; loud and happy.
fonts.avoid: Anything but short titles; all-caps runs over 3 words.

fonts.character: Bodoni with optical sizes: extreme contrast, fashion, opera houses, 1920s Paris métro posters.
fonts.avoid: Below 20 px at display opsz; on low-DPI dark grounds (hairlines break).

fonts.character: 19th-century 'fat face' didone: bold editorial headlines, broadsides, playbills.
fonts.avoid: Small sizes; it is ubiquitous on the web, give it a specific job.

fonts.character: Softened high-contrast display serif with a fine italic: magazine covers, elegant but friendly.
fonts.avoid: Bold (none); long titles.

fonts.character: Late-19th-century 'modern' text face: scientific journals, old newspapers, encyclopedia pages.
fonts.avoid: Small sizes on dark grounds; thin serifs.

fonts.character: A variable blackletter with roman bones: gothic flavour that stays readable; beer labels, Rhine towns, heraldry.
fonts.avoid: All-caps (blackletter caps must never be set in runs); body text.

fonts.character: Tiny 5 px pixel caps: arcade HUDs, LCD labels, game-cartridge stickers.
fonts.avoid: Sizes not a multiple of its grid (8/16/24 px); anything longer than a kicker.

fonts.character: DEC VT320 terminal bitmap: green-phosphor terminals, library catalogues, airport boards.
fonts.avoid: Body text; small sizes (it is small for its em, set ≥ 18 px).

fonts.character: Dot-matrix display face with a roundness axis: departure boards, receipt printers, LED clocks.
fonts.avoid: Below 24 px (dots merge); long words.

fonts.character: Letters built from modular elements (squares, hearts, circles) by axes: embroidery, LED signs, cross-stitch.
fonts.avoid: Body; fancy element shapes at small sizes.

fonts.character: Plump, italic, Gujarati-inspired display: 1970s diner signs, candy wrappers, disco record sleeves.
fonts.avoid: More than one line; next to other script faces.

fonts.character: Vertical-signage caps from urban street signs: bold, geometric, layered-colour ready; bodegas, cinemas.
fonts.avoid: Sentences; mixed case (caps only).

fonts.character: Art Deco display with thick-thin contrast: 1930s cinema marquees, cocktail bars, ocean liners.
fonts.avoid: Small sizes; anything not a title.

fonts.character: Hairline geometric Deco: Parisian boutiques, 1925 exhibition posters, very thin and airy.
fonts.avoid: Below 28 px or on dark grounds (single weight, thin); it fails contrast in spirit even when ratio passes.

fonts.character: Caps from Roman inscriptions: stone, monuments, museum plaques; carved, formal, timeless.
fonts.avoid: Lowercase does not exist (small caps only); epic-fantasy cliché when paired with gold on black.

fonts.character: Casual marker handwriting: fridge notes, shopping lists, a label on a jam jar.
fonts.avoid: Body, controls, anything read quickly; ≈67 KB per weight.

fonts.character: Brushier Caveat: chalkboard menus, market stall signs.
fonts.avoid: Everything but a kicker or a sticker; heavy file (≈100 KB).

fonts.character: Marker-drawn sans with an Informal axis and optional bounce: comic-book lettering you can still read in paragraphs.
fonts.avoid: BNCE (bounce) axis in body; ≈68 KB per weight; very long text.

fonts.character: Japanese pencil-textbook hand (from Fontworks) with matching Latin: a kissa menu written at the counter.
fonts.avoid: Body in Latin (its Latin is secondary); expecting weights between 400 and 600.

fonts.character: Tall x-height code face: clear, modern, reliable for times, codes and tables.
fonts.avoid: Being the whole personality of a theme.

fonts.character: Colophon's 1960s-flavoured mono: squarish, idiosyncratic caps; spacecraft manuals, zines.
fonts.avoid: Long paragraphs; it is overused on 'crypto' sites, give it print context.

fonts.character: Courier fixed for screens: typewriters, screenplays, ration cards, the bureau; honest and slightly analogue.
fonts.avoid: Tables of numbers (wide, slow to scan); pairing with Special Elite-style grunge.

fonts.character: Narrow mono with a cursive italic: compact tables, secretarial notes; the italic is a delight for labels.
fonts.avoid: Its cursive italic for numbers; ligatures in times.

fonts.character: Wide, squarish mono with a width axis: control panels, spacecraft telemetry, bold labels.
fonts.avoid: Long strings in narrow columns (it is wide).

fonts.character: Quirky slab-serif mono with a flowing italic: poetry chapbooks, library index cards.
fonts.avoid: Being the only weight you need for numbers-heavy screens.

fonts.character: Monospaced cousin of US Highway Gothic signage: transit timetables, road atlases.
fonts.avoid: Pairing with Overpass sans (too much of one voice).

fonts.character: Chicago industrial signage, condensed and tall: railway yards, stencilled crates, city hall banners.
fonts.avoid: Body; wide tracking at black weight.

fonts.character: Revival of Alternate Gothic No.1: 1900s newspapers, boxing posters, cinema listings.
fonts.avoid: Lowercase-heavy long titles; small sizes.

fonts.character: Californian highway-sign rounded grotesque, condensed: transit, dashboards, sports scoreboards.
fonts.avoid: Body paragraphs (fine for list rows, not reading).

fonts.character: Extremely condensed caps: tall, dramatic, film titles and fight cards.
fonts.avoid: Anything under 36 px; more than a few words.

fonts.character: Space-saving Plex: compact themes, dense lists and tables, control-room density with good legibility.
fonts.avoid: Airy themes (it looks cramped with generous space).

fonts.character: Very wide rounded-square display: bold, sporty, contemporary poster type.
fonts.avoid: Long titles in French (it runs wide); ≈66 KB per weight.

fonts.character: Heavy, wide Japanese-gothic display with Latin: manga covers, Shōwa-era shop signs, stamps.
fonts.avoid: More than a word or two; tracking it tight.

fonts.character: Wide 1900s Swedish-poster grotesque: sturdy, flat, generous; ferry timetables, enamel signs.
fonts.avoid: Body; tight tracking.

fonts.character: Width axis from ultra-condensed to extra-expanded: one family for tall headlines or wide banners, 80s-video-game energy at the extremes.
fonts.avoid: Using both extremes in the same theme.

fonts.character: Slightly rounded Californian highway-sign grotesque: stations, timetables, enamel signs; reads well at 14 px.
fonts.avoid: Barlow Condensed as its only contrast; a grotesque display beside it flattens both.

fonts.character: Japanese 16-dot bitmap gothic with Latin: 16-bit game menus, HUD counters, handheld LCDs.
fonts.avoid: Body text; sizes off its 16 px grid blur the dots.

fonts.character: Soft, puffy rounded letters like inflated stickers: toys, candy wrappers, keychain pets.
fonts.avoid: Anything longer than a title; another rounded face as the body's only contrast.

fonts.character: A neo-grotesque in monospace: Swiss precision for times, counts and the dimension figures of a drawing.
fonts.avoid: Needing bold (400 only); a humanist body beside it, which makes it look stiff.

fonts.character: Chunky pixel letters on a 15-unit grid: a jersey number, an LED scoreboard, a modular poster.
fonts.avoid: Body text and small labels; sizes that aren't a whole multiple of its grid.

fonts.character: Squared, technical mono with cut corners: console readouts, LCD players, sci-fi dashboards.
fonts.avoid: Paragraphs; another squared tech face beside it.

fonts.character: The M+ Japanese gothic as a mono: quiet, even and light; the stamped figures of a ledger or a timetable.
fonts.avoid: Display sizes (it is plain); its heavy weights on a paper texture.

fonts.character: Extended squared sans in the Microgramma tradition: chrome hi-fi, sci-fi consoles, Y2K media players.
fonts.avoid: More than a short title (very wide: French wraps); expecting other weights (400 only).

fonts.character: Sans with rounded terminals that stays legible at 14 px: friendly and toy-box warm without being childish.
fonts.avoid: Serious or civic themes; another rounded face beside it.

fonts.character: A pixel sans with real weights: handheld games, LCD screens, stickers on a handmade homepage.
fonts.avoid: Body paragraphs; sizes off its pixel grid, which smear the pixels.

fonts.character: Japanese mincho with a refined Latin: brush-tipped serifs, washi and sumi ink, quiet book titles.
fonts.avoid: Small Latin body text (the hairlines thin out); its heavy weights on dark grounds.

fonts.character: Clean Japanese gothic with a calm Latin: a small file, an even colour, reads at 14 px under a mincho.
fonts.avoid: Being the theme's only voice (it is plain); tight tracking.
